detailed_description: The CSS Minifier compresses pasted CSS text in the browser with simple string replacements. It removes block comments, collapses whitespace, removes spacing around common CSS punctuation, drops trailing semicolons before closing braces, removes units from zero values, and shortens matching six-digit hex colors when possible. After clicking Minify, the tool shows original size, minified size, and percentage saved, then lets you copy the readonly output. It does not parse CSS with a full standards engine, preserve selected comments, validate syntax, or provide production build optimization.
usage_steps: Paste CSS into the input textarea or edit the sample code.
Click Minify to remove comments and compact common CSS spacing.
Review the original size, minified size, and size reduction statistics.
Copy the minified CSS from the output textarea when needed.
usage_examples: Compact a small CSS snippet before pasting it into a demo or documentation page.
Remove comments and extra whitespace from copied CSS while checking the size difference.
Test how simple zero-unit and hex-color shortening affect a local CSS sample.
Copy a minified version of pasted CSS for a quick prototype after reviewing the output.
